publicationStmt.p: Tag layer of the DHSS Meta-Tagging Project. The article text is reproduced from the staged copy named in sourceDesc and is not altered; the tags are held separately in standOff so that overlapping and nested spans are preserved.

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: method
span.quote: We introduce a stochastic variational inference and learning algorithm that scales to large datasets and, under some mild differentiability conditions, even works in the intractable case.

span.label: approximate posterior inference with continuous latent variables
span.quote: How can we perform efficient approximate inference and learning with directed probabilistic models whose continuous latent variables and/or parameters have intractable posterior distributions?

span.label: system-or-tool-building
span.quote: We trained generative models of images from the MNIST and Frey Face datasets3 and compared learning algorithms in terms of the variational lower bound, and the estimated marginal likelihood.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: the reparameterization trick: rewrite latent-variable sampling as a deterministic function of noise so the variational lower bound (ELBO) becomes differentiable and trainable by stochastic gradient descent
span.quote: a reparameterization of the variational lower bound yields a lower bound estimator that can be straightforwardly optimized using

span.label: The derivation assumes a fixed dataset for simplicity rather than the online or non-stationary case.
span.note: what this limits: the derivation as presented: OUR METHOD CAN BE APPLIED TO ONLINE, NON-STATIONARY SETTINGS ... BUT HERE WE ASSUME A FIXED DATASET FOR SIMPLICITY
span.quote: Note that our method can be applied to online, non-stationary settings, e.g. streaming data, but here we assume a fixed dataset for simplicity.

span.label: The marginal-likelihood evaluation only works for very low-dimensional latent spaces; estimates degrade beyond three latent variables.
span.note: what this limits: the marginal-likelihood numbers reported: they use 3 LATENT VARIABLES, because FOR HIGHER DIMENSIONAL LATENT SPACE THE ESTIMATES BECAME UNRELIABLE
span.quote: For the encoder and decoder we again used neural networks, this time with 100 hidden units, and 3 latent variables; for higher dimensional latent space the estimates became unreliable.

span.label: The approximate posterior is assumed Gaussian with diagonal covariance, and the paper argues in advance that this is a choice rather than a limitation.
span.note: what this limits: results obtained with this method: the approximate posterior is assumed to take an approximately Gaussian form with approximately diagonal covariance, which the authors call a simplifying choice and not a limitation of the method
span.quote: While there is much freedom in the form qφ(z|x), we’ll assume the true (but intractable) posterior takes on a approximate Gaussian form with an approximately diagonal covariance

span.label: The reconstruction criterion that gives the method its auto-encoding name is stated to be insufficient on its own for learning useful representations.
span.note: what this limits: an auto-encoding objective read as a representation-learning objective: the paper states it is well known that the reconstruction criterion is in itself not sufficient for learning useful representations
span.quote: However, it is well known that this reconstruction criterion is in itself not sufficient for learning useful representations

span.label: The guarantee is conditional on differentiability, which is assumed to hold almost everywhere rather than shown.
span.note: what this limits: the claim that the estimator works in the intractable case: it holds under mild differentiability conditions, with the prior and likelihood assumed to have PDFs differentiable almost everywhere
span.quote: We assume that the prior pθ∗ (z) and likelihood pθ∗ (x|z) come from parametric families of distributions pθ(z) and pθ(x|z), and that their PDFs are differentiable almost everywhere
